attractions.name: Red Fort (Muzaffarabad Fort)
attractions.description: A centuries-old fort overlooking the confluence of the Neelum and Jhelum rivers.

attractions.name: Neelum Valley
attractions.description: A stunning, forested river valley extending northeast from Muzaffarabad, considered one of the most scenic areas in Pakistan-administered Kashmir.

attractions.name: Pir Chinasi
attractions.description: A mountain shrine and viewpoint offering panoramic views over Muzaffarabad and the surrounding valleys.

food_places.name: Local trout restaurants (Neelum Valley route)
food_places.specialty: Fresh river trout from Neelum Valley streams

transportation.notes: Recommended for exploring the Neelum Valley road

accommodations.name: Mid-range hotel near the river confluence

weather_info.climate_type: Humid subtropical highland climate, cooler than the plains due to elevation and river valleys
weather_info.avoid_months: Heavy winter snowfall can restrict access to upper Neelum Valley

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Cold, occasional snowfall, especially in upper valley areas

travel_tips.tip: The Neelum Valley road follows the river closely and offers some of the most scenic driving in the region, but can be narrow in places -- drive carefully.
Hire a local jeep or car for Neelum Valley trips, as public transport options are limited further up the valley.
Check current road conditions before heading into the Neelum Valley, especially after heavy rain or in winter.
Visit between April and October for the best combination of pleasant weather and open mountain roads.

history.founded: Historically linked to the broader Kashmir region, with the city taking its current name from Sultan Muzaffar Khan in the 18th century
history.city_history: Muzaffarabad has served as the capital of Azad Jammu & Kashmir since the region's formation in 1947, following the partition of British India and the Kashmir conflict. The city sits at the confluence of the Neelum and Jhelum rivers and serves as the gateway to the scenic Neelum Valley.
history.province_history: Azad Jammu & Kashmir is a self-governing territory of Pakistan, formed in 1947 in the aftermath of the partition of British India and the subsequent Kashmir conflict, distinct from the neighboring Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir.
